subject: Citrine Health security questionnaire: PII handling, KMS custody, telemetry lockbox
messages:
From: Carlos Gomez <security@citrinehealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Security questionnaire + DPA annex asks (PII handling, KMS custody)

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for taking this — Citrine Health is progressing toward an integration pilot with Redwood and our InfoSec team has a handful of items we need answered before we can sign the DPA annex. Attached is our baseline security questionnaire (SSQ) and a short DPA checklist. High-level asks:

- Clarify PII classification and how PHI/PII is segmented at ingress.
- Evidence of KMS custody options (customer-owned keys vs. vendor-managed) and an attestation if available.
- Typical telemetry retention windows for inference requests and any options to minimize telemetry (esp. streaming tokens).
- A process for lockboxed subprocessor access if we need to limit pre-production access to raw prompts.

Can you confirm the best way to proceed? We can either route answers in the spreadsheet or schedule a 30-min call next week with engineering.

Attachments: citrine_ssq_v1.xlsx (xlsx), dpa-request.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Carlos Gomez
Security Lead — Citrine Health
security@citrinehealth.com

Subject: Re: Security questionnaire + DPA annex asks (PII handling, KMS custody)

Carlos — thanks for the clear list. We're excited to move this forward. Quick proposal: we can (A) fill the SSQ with annotated answers and artifacts, or (B) run a 30-minute technical call to walk your team through the dataflow and KMS options. I'm happy to do both.

Short answers / pointers to save time:
- PII classification: Redwood supports per-customer field mappings. Ingested fields marked as PII/PHI in the mapping are segmented at the routing layer and tracked in the access control registry. Default policy is least-privilege read for inference paths; only roles with explicit PII access flags can retrieve de-pseudonymized content.

- Telemetry retention: Hosted API telemetry (request/response metadata, traces) is retained 30 days by default. For Dedicated/Private deployments we support configurable retention down to 7 days; we also offer an opt-down option that excludes streaming token payloads from persisted logs.

- KMS custody: three modes: 1) Redwood-managed keys (hosted) — default, 2) Customer-managed keys via our KMS proxy (supported for Dedicated and Private), 3) HSM-backed BYOK for on-prem/private installs. We have an attestation (HSM/KMS) that we can share — see attachment from Lauren.

- Lockbox for subprocessors: we operate a short-term lockbox process for evaluation environments where raw prompts are vetted and access is timeboxed. That process requires a subprocessor roster + justification, and we provide an audit snapshot once the window closes. Ben is looping in to provide current subprocessors and lockbox playbook.

Next steps:
1) I will provide draft SSQ answers (annotated spreadsheet) + artifacts.
2) Lauren will attach the KMS attestation and an annotated dataflow.
3) Ben will provide the subprocessor roster and describe how lockbox sessions are scheduled.

Would you prefer the docs first or a call? If call: propose Wed 11/11 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu 11/12 08:00–08:30 PT.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
ikhil_sharma@redwood.com

Carlos — looping in with the artifacts and a concise technical write-up to drop into the SSQ. Attached: kms-attestation-2026-09.pdf and dataflow-annotated.svg. Also uploaded an annotated dataflow to the shared drive (link below).

High-level technical notes you can paste into the SSQ:
- Dataflow (ingest -> routing -> runtime -> ephemeral cache -> output): ingest endpoints accept configurable field-level markers; routing attaches a tenant tag which drives isolation. KV cache is encrypted per-tenant and is not persisted to long-term object storage in hosted mode.

- KMS modes and evidence:
  * Redwood-managed keys: we perform envelope encryption; keys rotate quarterly; key material stored in our KMS backed by cloud provider HSMs. Suitable for most pilots.
  * Customer-managed KMS proxy: customer provides key material in their KMS; we perform remote attestation and use a proxy to call customer's KMS for envelope operations. Supported for Dedicated/Private.
  * HSM BYOK: for private/on-prem we can integrate with customer HSM (PKCS#11).

- Attestation scope: attached PDF is our vendor KMS/HSM attestation (covers rotation, split keys, and key-zeroization procedures). If Citrine needs a customer-specific KMS integration test report we can generate a scoped proof of concept with a short security-runbook (2–3 days).

- Telemetry: default retention 30 days. For Dedicated/Private we expose retention configuration and can exclude streaming token payloads from persisted logs. We also support a minimal telemetry mode for test pilots where only request metadata and error traces are persisted.

- Lockbox (subprocessor access reduction): process summary:
  1) Citrine requests a lockbox window and provides justification + list of accounts/devs that need access.
  2) Redwood schedules a timeboxed environment (mirrored sandbox) and enables redaction + tokenization on ingest.
  3) Access is provisioned via short-lived credentials; all sessions audited and a post-window audit snapshot provided.

Attachments: kms-attestation-2026-09.pdf (pdf), dataflow-annotated.svg (svg)
Drive link: https://drive.redwood/reports/citrine-dataflow-annotated

Happy to turn these bullets into SSQ cells — say the word and I'll upload the completed spreadsheet.

— Lauren
Principal Security Architect — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
